The DPLL algorithm

Source: R/logic-inference.R
dpll_satisfiable.Rd

The building blocks of the Davis Putnam Logemann Loveland algorithm in sympy.logic.algorithms.dpll: dpll_satisfiable(expr) returns a model (a named list) or FALSE; dpll(clauses, symbols, model) searches from a partial model; find_pure_symbol(), find_unit_clause() and unit_propagate() are its steps. The _int_repr variants work on clauses given as integer vectors (positive and negative literals), and to_int_repr(clauses, symbols) encodes clauses so; pl_true_int_repr() evaluates one such clause.

Usage

dpll_satisfiable(expr)

dpll(clauses, symbols, model)

find_pure_symbol(symbols, unknown_clauses)

find_unit_clause(clauses, model)

unit_propagate(clauses, symbol)

to_int_repr(clauses, symbols)

pl_true_int_repr(clause, model = list())

unit_propagate_int_repr(clauses, s)

find_pure_symbol_int_repr(symbols, unknown_clauses)

find_unit_clause_int_repr(clauses, model)

dpll_int_repr(clauses, symbols, model)

Arguments

expr

A boolean expression.

clauses

A list of clauses.

symbols

A list of symbols, or an integer vector.

model

A named list of logical values (keyed by symbol names, or by integers for the _int_repr functions).

unknown_clauses

A list of clauses.

symbol

A literal.

clause

An integer clause.

s

An integer literal.

Value

A model, FALSE, a pair list(symbol, value) or a list of clauses.

Examples

A <- Symbol("A"); B <- Symbol("B")
dpll_satisfiable(And(A, Not(B)))
#> $B
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $A
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
find_pure_symbol(list(A, B), list(Or(A, Not(B)), Or(Not(B), A)))
#> [[1]]
#> A
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
unit_propagate(list(Or(A, B), Or(Not(A), B)), A)
#> [[1]]
#> B
#>
